body:
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL | AAPL Price Prediction) and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) both report fresh numbers on July 30, 2026, and their last quarters set up a fascinating split. Apple leaned on iPhone 17 demand and a services flywheel. Amazon leaned on AWS reacceleration and a giant AI capex bet. Two very different playbooks, one shared earnings night.

## iPhone 17 Carries Apple. AWS Carries Amazon. [...] Apple’s Q2 FY26 delivered $111.18B in revenue, up 16.6% YoY, with iPhone alone contributing $56.99B and Services hitting an all-time record of $30.98B. Tim Cook credited “extraordinary demand for the iPhone 17 lineup”, alongside the MacBook Neo launch. It was Apple’s eighth consecutive EPS beat.

Apple reported third-quarter sales and profits that topped analysts’ estimates.

The company said its fiscal third-quarter revenue jumped 16% year-over-year to $109.4 billion, ahead of the $108.2 billion analysts expected. Earnings per share, at $2.02, beat the Street consensus compiled by Visible Alpha of $1.87. [...] Amazon’s revenue increased 20% to $200.6 billion in the second quarter, easily beating the $196.8 billion Wall Street expected. Earnings grew 245% to $62.65 billion, or $5.15 a share, far surpassing estimates. (Amazon’s quarterly profit got a $53.4 billion boost from “other income,” much of it tied to its investments in AI lab Anthropic.) [...] Apple said its gross margin, which came in at 50.1%, above the Street’s estimate near 48%, got a roughly 2 percentage-point lift from tariff refunds.

Earnings per share were also 5% higher, benefitting to the tune of $0.11 from refunds for tariffs that were struck down by the Supreme Court earlier this year.

—Kara Greenberg
